title: Wonders of the world
examples: Which wonder is in the mountains?
Can you tell me about the Great Wall?
Where can I see the Colosseum?

explain.say: Today we say about some amazing old places. We will learn about four great wonders. These are the Great Wall, Petra, Machu Picchu, and the Colosseum.

draw.text: Wonders: Great Wall, Petra, Machu Picchu, Colosseum

explain.say: The Great Wall is a very long wall in China. It was built to protect the country long ago. It shows great engineering skill.

draw.text: Great Wall: Long protection wall in China

explain.say: Petra is a city carved into pink rock walls. People used it for trade many years ago. It looks very magical.
Machu Picchu is a lost city high in the mountains. The Inca people built it there. It has amazing views all around.

draw.text: Machu Picchu: Inca city in Peruvian mountains

explain.say: The Colosseum was a huge stadium in Rome. People held big shows and events there. It was very famous for entertainment.
Imagine you are visiting a place with these wonders. You might see the Great Wall stretching over hills. You might also see the Colosseum standing tall in a city center.

draw.text: Comparing wonders: Great Wall vs Colosseum

faq.q: Are all these places still standing today?
faq.a: Yes, many of these wonderful sites are still visible today. People can visit and see the history for themselves. You might also ask: Are they ruins? Or: Can I see them now?

faq.q: Why are some of them harder to see?
faq.a: Some structures are very old, so nature has changed them over time. This makes them look different from how they first appeared. You might also ask: Are they damaged? Or: What happened to them?

faq.q: Were these built by the same group of people?
faq.a: No, each wonder was built by different civilizations. The builders were different groups of people. You might also ask: Who built them? Or: Were they from one culture?
The Great Wall is known for being incredibly long. It stretches across a massive area of land. You can imagine its huge size.
asks: Which one is the longest structure?

faq.q: What material was Petra made from?
faq.a: Petra was famous for being carved directly out of natural rock. This gives it a unique pink color. It is a natural wonder too.

faq.q: What was the purpose of the Colosseum?
faq.a: The Colosseum was primarily used for large public shows and events. It was a place for entertainment for the Roman people. It was a massive venue.

faq.q: What is the main difference between Machu Picchu and the others?
faq.a: Machu Picchu is unique because it is built high up in the mountains. This gives it a special, isolated setting. It is surrounded by dramatic peaks.

facts: The Great Wall is a series of fortifications built across the historical northern borders of China.
Petra is famous for its rock-cut architecture, which was used by Nabataeans.
Machu Picchu was a citadel set high in the Andes Mountains in modern-day Peru.
The Colosseum in Rome hosted gladiatorial contests and public spectacles.

quiz.say: Which wonder is known for its pink rock carvings?
quiz.why: Petra is specifically famous for being carved into natural rock walls.

wrong.0: Machu Picchu is a city built on terraces, not carved into rock.
wrong.1: The Colosseum was a large stadium structure, not carved from rock.
wrong.3: The Great Wall is built of stone and earth, not carved from rock.

quiz.say: If you needed a very long defensive barrier, which wonder would you study?
quiz.why: The Great Wall is recognized globally for its immense length as a border defense.

wrong.0: The Colosseum was an arena for events, not a border wall.
wrong.2: Petra is known for its carvings, not its length as a barrier.
wrong.3: Machu Picchu is a city site, not a defensive wall.

quiz.say: Which site was a massive stadium for Roman shows?
quiz.why: The Colosseum's entire purpose was to host large public spectacles and games.

wrong.0: The Great Wall was built for defense, not for public shows.
wrong.2: Machu Picchu was a residential and religious citadel, not an arena.
wrong.3: Petra was a trade center carved into rock, not a stadium.
